content: Flat-file CMS options (Bludit, Kirby, WonderCMS, Automad, SiteCake) let non-technical owners edit content without a database, but all require installing and maintaining another PHP application on the host. For a small 10-15 page brochure site, the simpler and lower-risk pattern is: keep content in per-page PHP/HTML files with clearly delimited editable sections plus a short editing guide -- avoids adding an admin panel attack surface for content that changes rarely.
